intro: An Akkadian collection of Babylonian prescriptions for restoring a man's sexual potency (ŠÀ.ZI.GA, literally 'rising of the heart'), copied at Ḫattuša. Most remedies use parts of animals associated with sexual vigour (a male partridge caught in a set month, an aroused bull, ram or billy-goat, mating geckos, a stag's horn), dried and crushed and then given in beer or water, rubbed on with oil or tied on the hips. A fragment of a Sumerian incantation follows, and the edges carry a further recipe and a subscript naming the tablet as the second(?) of the series 'If a man … potency'.

sections.title: Additional recipe on the edges; subscript

paras.en: If a man (seeks) potency: in the month Nisannu, at (its) end(?), you catch a male partridge. You pluck its wings, strangle it and flatten(?) it; you sprinkle salt (on it) and dry (it). You crush (it) together with seed of the mountain GÍR.ḪAB-thorn and give it to him to drink in beer, and that man will have potency.

Ditto: a male partridge that is aroused to mount (the female) you dry and crush; you throw (it) into water of (i.e. left on?) the roof … (bu-ut-tu, meaning unclear) and give it to him to drink, and that man will have potency.

Ditto: a male partridge — you cut off its head and let its blood fall into water; you swallow(?) its heart, and that water you leave overnight under the stars. When the sun comes up you give it to him to drink, and he will have potency.

Ditto: the penis of a male partridge, the froth of an aroused bull, the froth of an aroused ram — you give (it) to him to drink in water. And in … (saḫr[at …]) you wrap (it) in wool from the thigh(?) of a sheep, [and] put (it) on the … (BÁR.KA), and he will have potency.

Ditto: you pluck an AL.DI.RÍ.GA-bird and sprinkle (it); you smear it with salt (and) the nīnû-plant (Ú.KUR.RA), dry (it) and crush (it). You mix (it) with flour of roasted grain and give it to him to drink, and he will have potency.

Ditto: you pluck a NAM.GEŠTIN-bird and sprinkle (it); you smear (it) with amānu-salt (and) the nīnû-plant, and crush (it). … grain(?), flour of roasted grain, (and) the mountain [GÍ]R.ḪAB-thorn — you give it to him [to d]rink on an empty stomach, and he will have potency.
Ditto: the 'dog's tongue'-plant (EME.UR.KU) you …; you give it to him to drink, and he will have poten[cy].

Ditto: the wing of a male eagle, the wing of an i[girû]-bird(?), mating field geck[os], the dung of a GAR.IB-bird, the dung of a speckled lizard, se[ed of the MA.NU-tree, seed of the IN.NU.UŠ-plant, seed of the azallû-plant, seed of the MUL.DÙ.DÙ-plant], seed of the 'dog's tongue'-plant, the šakirû-plant, ṣaṣ[untu], the SUMUN.DAR-plant: these 14 plants(?) you crush(?) together, mix with coarse flour and form into pel[lets]. You make three kuppatinnu-(pellets); among the kuppatinnu-(pellets) you ma[ke] …; all (of it?) on an empty stomach you … ; to the kuppitannu(?) … you bind (it) on your hips … potenc[y].
Ditto: wh[en …] (traces; a gap of about six lines) … you ta[ke] … you give it to him to drink, and …
Ditto: when a ram … the wool of its tail … its thread(?) … (ri-ta-tu[m]) … on [his] hi[ps] … (a blank line follows)
Ditto: wh[en …] the heart of a partri[dge], the spittle(?) of an aroused bull … on the roof, (exposed) to the stars … when the sun has ri[sen] … they stood(?) t[o …] in […]
Ditt[o]: … of a [mounting](?) dog you dry and crush and …; you mix (it) and give it to him to drink in water, [and] he will have potency.

Ditto: the 'mounting' (i.e. the mating secretion?) of a GAR.IB-bird, the eli[…]-plant, tertennu(?), tamarisk, the IN.NU.UŠ-plant, date palm, the KAN.Ḫ[U+SI]-tree(?) and all (kinds of) seeds you throw into water; you leave (it) overnight under the stars; you set (it) on the roof. That man (is) seated; with water (and) the k[asû-plant] you rin[se] his whole body. The 'mounting' of a GAR.IB-bird: half he drinks, and hal[f] … (ni šìr) and terte[nnu] … on his left(?) foot … water … you crush, and with p[ure] oil you anoint him repeatedly, and the m[an …].
Ditto: the skull(?) of a partri[dge] … [with pure oil] you anoint [his body] repeatedly, and the m[an …].

Ditto: (if?) potency (lit. 'lifting of the heart') has turned(?): the penis of a par[tridge] (and) flesh of the throat(?) of a ram you wrap up and place on (his) hips, [and] that man (will have) potency.
Ditto: a field gec[ko] … in front … you make … [o]n an empty stomach … he will have potency.
[… arou]sed(?) …, the horn of a stag … [poten]cy.
[…] … you bind (it) […]
If a man (whose) pot[ency …] whe[n …]
Ditto: a man who[se] po[tency …] with … [is ab]le(?) … the 'potency'-plant (Ú.ŠÀ.ZI.GA) … potency … if with … for his potency … the KASKAL.MUNUS(?)-plant … you receive(?) … ra-… [potency].
[Traces only.]
… the GÙN(?).KUR.RA … you bind (it), and … [poten]cy.

[Sumerian incantation, fragmentary and not understood in detail: '… (te-en-te-en, "be calm"?) … favourable(?) … favourable(?) … rise, rise(?) …', closing with the incantation formula é-nu-ru (= én-nu-ru).]

[Wh]en the partridge (iṣṣūr ḫurri) keeps mounting, you [catch] a male [partri]dge in the month Ayyaru. You do not discard(?) the blood; their intestines … not … water …; you … (teḫil) and, whether two months(?) or … (ṣupri appi karši: 'claw(?), tip(?), belly(?)'), the sinews and the intestines you crush with (lit. in) stones and decoct (them). Three handfuls of seed of the aluzinnu-plant (and) two handfuls of ḫu-… you mix; in beer, as usual(?), you beat (it up) and give it to him to drink on an empty stomach, and the ma[n] will be aroused (lit. 'will lift'). [The hea]rt of a male raven(?), the blood of an aroused billy-goat, a male [part]ridge, the 'mounting' of a GAR.IB-bird (and) seed of the GÍR.ḪAB-thorn you mix together; you anoint the man's … (〈GIŠ〉.KUN, perhaps the penis) three times(?), and he will have potency. Incantation-rubric: potency. Tablet 2(?) (of the series) 'If a man … potency'.
